What an Automated Payroll System for Small Business Changes and What Stays Yours
Automating payroll changes how data moves between your time records, HR files, tax deposits, and year-end forms. When a payroll service provider or reporting agent deposits taxes and prepares or files returns for you, the IRS says the employer remains liable. Every handoff you automate still needs a check you own.
Five handoffs make up a pay run, and each has a rule behind it
A pay run is a chain of handoffs, and each handoff is a place where a number is retyped, pasted, or passed to someone else. Multi-system payroll processing means a pay run draws on more than one source, such as time records, HR files, a payroll tool or spreadsheet, tax accounts, and year-end forms. The chain has five links.


* Move approved hours from the time record into payroll.
* Enter HR data such as new hires, withholding forms, support orders, and direct deposit choices.
* Send withheld taxes out as deposits and returns.
* Furnish and file year-end forms.
* Carry year-to-date balances from one system to another when you switch.


Software can carry data across a handoff. The rule behind each handoff, and the check on its result, stay with the employer.
Why the case against Excel rests on the handoffs
Under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the federal wage-and-hour law, the Department of Labor (DOL) says the Act requires no particular form for payroll records, so the case against Excel does not rest on file format. In our view, it rests on the handoffs around the file.


A spreadsheet holds whatever is typed or pasted into it, so each added location, pay schedule, or time source can add another place where hours are copied by hand. The IRS publishes withholding tables for both automated and manual payroll systems in Publication 15-T, so a spreadsheet and an automated system both apply IRS withholding methods. The difference is who moves the numbers, not which rules apply. For payroll automation for small business, whether a provider connects the systems that feed a pay run, and who tests that connection, are questions to put to the provider in writing.


Overtime and pay-practice rules vary by industry and state. Confirm the ones that apply to you with the Department of Labor or your state labor agency.


Asure Time & Attendance sends approved hours into payroll once managers approve them, flags exceptions, and sends overtime alerts, with shared data on AsureCentral.
HR data changes what payroll pays and what you must report
New hires, withholding forms, support orders, and direct deposit choices each carry a rule that changes what payroll pays or reports. An employer should have a signed Form W-4, the federal withholding certificate, on file for each employee, and Publication 15 tells employers to ask new employees for one when they start work and to make it effective with the first wage payment.


According to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), a new-hire report goes to a state agency, not the IRS, within 20 days of hire, and some states require it sooner. An employer must honor a valid income withholding for support order. DOL enforcement guidance accepts direct deposit provided employees have the option of receiving cash or check directly from the employer, and states may add rules, so check with your state labor agency.


Each of these arrives from an employee, an agency, or HR. In a spreadsheet, a person has to remember each one. Whether a given system or provider carries each one is a question to confirm in writing.
The tax handoff ends with a check you own
The IRS tells employers who use a payroll provider to register for their own Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) PIN and periodically verify payments. The employer applies the withholding methods in Publication 15-T, or an automated system built on them. Deposits must be made electronically, and a payroll service or other third party can make them on your behalf.


According to the IRS third party arrangements page, a payroll service provider prepares returns for you to sign under your employer identification number (EIN), while a reporting agent authorized on Form 8655 signs and generally e-files separate returns under your EIN.


Treat the first missed payment by a provider as a red flag, and keep the IRS address of record as your business’s own rather than the provider’s. A reporting agent must give clients a written statement each quarter that the employer is responsible for filing and paying on time, under Internal Revenue Manual 5.1.24. If you suspect improper or fraudulent payroll service provider activity involving deposits or returns, you can file Form 14157.


As of October 2026, failure-to-deposit penalties are set as a percentage of the unpaid deposit, at 2% when 1 to 5 days late, 5% when 6 to 15 days late, 10% when more than 15 days late, and 15% when still unpaid more than 10 days after the first IRS notice or on the day you receive a notice demanding immediate payment. The tiers replace one another rather than add, and the IRS may remove or reduce penalties for reasonable cause.


Form 941 is the quarterly federal employment tax return. Employers with multiple locations or divisions file only one Form 941 per quarter, per IRS Publication 15. The rule applies per EIN, so each entity with its own EIN files its own Form 941.
Year-end forms and changing payroll systems mid-year both depend on year-to-date data
Year-end forms and a mid-year switch both depend on knowing what has already been paid this year. As of October 2026, Form W-2 reports wages paid during the calendar year, and using a payroll service provider or reporting agent does not relieve the employer of furnishing Forms W-2 to employees and filing Forms W-2 and W-3 with the Social Security Administration. The 2026 forms are due February 1, 2027, and Publication 15-A allows electronic delivery of a W-2 only to an employee who has consented.


Two caps depend on year-to-date wages. As of October 2026, social security tax is 6.2% each for employer and employee on wages up to a $184,500 wage base. FUTA, the federal unemployment tax, applies to the first $7,000 paid to each employee at 6.0%, less a credit of up to 5.4% for state unemployment tax paid in full and on time, per IRS Publication 15 and the Form 940 instructions.


In a hypothetical example, an employee is paid $150,000 before the switch and $150,000 after, and no year-to-date balances are loaded into the new system. Together the two systems withhold social security on the full $300,000 ($18,600.00 at 6.2%) instead of stopping at the $184,500 base ($11,439.00), an over-withholding of $7,161.00. The employer’s matching share overshoots by the same amount.


In our view, a mid-year start needs the year-to-date balances loaded first, because the two caps above cannot be applied correctly without them. A quarter boundary, year end, and a mid-year start with a year-to-date load are planning options for you and your provider to weigh against your filing calendar.


Form 941-X corrects a filed Form 941. Underreported tax must be corrected by the due date of the return for the quarter in which you find the error, and you pay what is owed when you file.
What to ask when you replace Excel payroll with software
A feature list tells you what a system can do, and these questions, put to any provider in writing, tell you who does what, from payroll software integration with time tracking to year-end forms.


* Ask how approved hours reach payroll (a built-in connection, an API, or a file import) and who sets up and tests it.
* Ask who files each return under whose EIN, and whether the provider acts as a payroll service provider or as a reporting agent on Form 8655.
* Confirm that you keep your own EFTPS or Business Tax Account access and your own IRS address of record, and ask whether you receive the quarterly written statement a reporting agent must provide.
* Ask which changes employees can make in self-service and which need administrator approval before they reach payroll.
* Get in writing who exports, loads, and checks year-to-date balances in a mid-year start.
* Ask whether one login can hold a separate company setup for each EIN, and how deposits and returns stay attached to the right one.
* Confirm whether W-2 preparation, filing, and delivery are in the base fee and how employee consent for electronic W-2s is collected.
Frequently Asked Questions
Does Excel meet federal payroll record rules?
A spreadsheet can hold payroll records under the FLSA, which requires no particular form for them. The FLSA requires payroll records for at least three years and records on which wage computations are based, such as time cards, for at least two years, per DOL Fact Sheet 21. The IRS requires employment tax records for at least four years, per Publication 15. State retention periods vary, so check with your state labor agency.
How do I confirm my payroll taxes were deposited?
Check your own IRS account rather than relying only on a provider’s report. EFTPS shows 16 months of payment history online, and an IRS Business Tax Account shows payment history if your business is eligible. Contact the IRS promptly about any bill or notice caused by a provider problem.
Who reports a new hire, and when?
Employers report each new employee to a state agency in the state where the employee works, not to the IRS, within 20 days of hire, and some states require it sooner. A rehire counts as new after at least 60 consecutive days of separation, per IRS Publication 15. The report carries seven data elements, the employee’s name, address, Social Security number, and date of hire, and the employer’s name, address, and federal employer identification number. A multistate employer may report to each work state or register with HHS and report all hires to one chosen state, per the HHS new hire reporting page. Ask your provider in writing whether it submits the report.
What do I do when I receive a child support withholding order?
Honor a valid income withholding for support order and send the payment no more than seven business days after paying wages, or sooner if your state sets a shorter time. Employers that do not withhold and send payments as ordered are subject to penalties in every state. Confirm in writing who withholds and who sends the payment when a provider runs your payroll.
Can I give employees their W-2s electronically?
Yes, but only to an employee who has consented, under IRS Publication 15-A. Before consent, the employee must be told that paper is the alternative, the scope and duration of the consent, how to get a paper copy, how to withdraw consent, what hardware and software are needed, and when electronic delivery ends. Electronic copies are due by the paper deadline, February 1, 2027 for 2026 forms, as of October 2026.
